blocks.TGeography.intro.0: Contains information about the geographic validity of the process. The geography may be the point location of the activity, a line describing a mobile activity, or an area of a distributed activity or of a production mix, containing several located activities. For markets (consumption mixes), the geography describes the market boundaries, across which imports and exports are limited.
blocks.TGeography.400.description.0: Reference to valid locations file with detailed geography information.
blocks.TGeography.401.description.0: Reference to the context of the geography.
blocks.TGeography.401.description.1: If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TGeography.410.description.0: Descriptive shortname of the location referenced by geographyId, e.g. the regional codes of EcoSpold version 1.
blocks.TGeography.420.description.0: Text and image field for further explanations of the geography. Especially for area descriptions, the nature of the geographical delimitation may be given, especially when this is not an administrative area. Justifications for market boundaries may also be provided here.Text and image fields are list of text, imageUri and variable elements. The text and imageUri elements can used to describe the current section and they can be combined in any order given by their index attribute. Text variables are defined by the variable elements, which may be used in the text as {{variablename}}. If a parent text field includes a variable, this variable may be redefined by the child activity dataset while keeping the rest of the parent text intact. This allows easy changes of text parts in child processes.
blocks.TGeography.420.description.1: List of text, imageUri and variable elements. The text and imageUri elements can used to describe the current section and they can be combined in any order given by their index attribute. Text variables are defined by the variable elements, which may be used in the text as {{variablename}}. If a parent text field includes a variable, this variable may be redefined by the child activity dataset while keeping the rest of the parent text intact. This allows easy changes of text parts in child processes.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.intro.0: Comprises fields (additional to the exchanges section) which are only valid for elementary exchanges. Exchanges with environment are elementary flows as inputs and outputs recorded in a unit process and its related information.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.intro.1: This section extends the exchanges section in case of exchanges with environment.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1600.description.0: Indicates the kind of input flow. The codes are: 4=From Environment
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1600.description.1: For each exchange only an inputGroup or outputGroup shall exist. This indicates the direction of the flow.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1600.description.2: This field is the equivalent of field 1500 with a different set of valid values.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1610.description.0: Indicates the kind of output flow. The codes are: 4=ToEnvironment
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1610.description.1: For each exchange only an inputGroup or outputGroup shall exist. This indicates the direction of the flow.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1610.description.2: This field is the equivalent of field 1510 with a different set of valid values.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1615.description.0: Reference to the master data entry for this elementary exchange
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1616.description.0: Reference to the context of the elementary exchange.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1616.description.1: If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1660.description.0: Name of the compartment and subcompartment of the exchange. The xml document referenced by validCompartments contains definitions of valid compartment/subcompartment pairs for a given language.
blocks.TElementaryExchange.1670.description.0: Chemical formula (e.g. sum formula) may be entered.
blocks.TCompartment.intro.0: Contains compartment pairs to specify an exchange.
blocks.TCompartment.330.description.0: The name of the compartment.This is the plaintext value of the referenced compartment (field 5315).
blocks.TCompartment.340.description.0: The name of the subcompartment.This is the plaintext value of the referenced subcompartment (field 5325).
blocks.TCompartment.350.description.0: Reference to the compartment/subcompartment pair. Must be defined in list of valid compartments (see field 5330).
blocks.TCompartment.351.description.0: Reference to the context of the subcompartment
blocks.TCompartment.351.description.1: If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TUncertainty.intro.0: Of the following uncertainty methods (lognormal, normal, ..., undefined) exactly one must be selected. The TUncertainty complex type is used in several places, so one dataset may contain several uncertainty elements in distinct places. But each element which has uncertainty may only contain one.
blocks.TUncertainty.2010.description.0: A general comment can be made about each uncertainty information
blocks.TUncertainty.2100.description.0: The Lognormal-distribution with average value μ (Mu parameter) and variance σ (Variance parameter) is a Normal-distribution, shaping the natural logarithm of the characteristic values ln(x) instead of x-values.
blocks.TUncertainty.2102.description.0: Arithmetic mean of the underlying normal distribution
blocks.TUncertainty.2103.description.0: Unbiased variance of the underlying normal distribution
blocks.TUncertainty.2104.description.0: Unbiased variance of the underlying normal distribution, basic uncertainty with pedigree uncertainty
blocks.TUncertainty.2110.description.0: Normal (also known as "Gaussian") distribution. It is a family of distributions of the same general form, differing in their location and scale parameters: the mean ("MeanValue") and standard deviation ("Deviation"), respectively.
blocks.TUncertainty.2113.description.0: Unbiased variance, basic uncertainty with pedigree uncertainty
blocks.TUncertainty.2120.description.1: In case of triangular uncertainty distribution, the meanValue shall be calculated from the mostLikelyValue. The field mostLikelyValue (#3797) must not be used in the ecoinvent context.
blocks.TUncertainty.2130.description.0: Uniform distribution of values between the minValue and the maxValue parameter. If the maxValue parameter is smaller than the minValue parameter their values will be swapped.
blocks.TUncertainty.2140.description.0: Beta distribution using minValue (a), maxValue (b) and mostFrequentValue (m) parameters to calculate the two shape parameters of the underlying Gamma distributions. The parameters must follow this condition: ((a <= m) and (m <= b)) or (a = b). The shape values will be calculated by these formulas: Shape1 = 1 + 4 * ((m-a) / (b-a)). Shape2 = 6 - Shape1.
blocks.TUncertainty.2150.description.0: Gamma distribution using scale and shape parameter. Absolute values of the values entered here will be used. The value of the minimum parameter will be added to all samples.
blocks.TUncertainty.2160.description.0: Binomial distribution using n and p parameter.
blocks.TUncertainty.2162.description.0: Probability of success in each trial
blocks.TUncertainty.2170.description.0: This "distribution" can be used to hold legacy data of the EcoSpold01 format which reused the minValue, maxValue and standardDeviation95 fields to store undefined distribution data.
blocks.TUncertainty.2173.description.0: The value, extended from both sides of the mean, that would be necessary to cover 95% of the population
blocks.TUncertainty.2270.description.0: The data quality indicators provides a qualitative assessment of data quality. This can be converted to a quantitative additional uncertainty, which can be added to the basic uncertainty. The pedigreeMatrix element groups the 5 data quality indicators and contains no data itself.
blocks.TUncertainty.2271.description.1: 2=Verified data partly based on assumptions OR nonverified data based on measurements
blocks.TUncertainty.2271.description.2: 3=Non-verified data partly based on qualified estimates
blocks.TUncertainty.2272.description.0: 1=Representative data from all sites relevant for the market considered over an adequate period to even out normal fluctuations
blocks.TUncertainty.2272.description.1: 2=Representative data from >50% of the sites relevant for the market considered over an adequate period to even out normal fluctuations
blocks.TUncertainty.2272.description.2: 3=Representative data from only some sites (<<50%) relevant for the market considered OR >50% of sites but from shorter periods
blocks.TUncertainty.2272.description.3: 4=Representative data from only one site relevant for the market considered OR some sites but from shorter periods
blocks.TUncertainty.2272.description.4: 5=Representativeness unknown or data from a small number of sites AND from shorter periods
blocks.TUncertainty.2273.description.0: 1=Less than 3 years of difference to the time period of the dataset (fields 600-610)
blocks.TUncertainty.2273.description.1: 2=Less than 6 years of difference to the time period of the dataset (fields 600-610)
blocks.TUncertainty.2273.description.2: 3=Less than 10 years of difference to the time period of the dataset (fields 600-610)
blocks.TUncertainty.2273.description.3: 4=Less than 15 years of difference to the time period of the dataset (fields 600-610)
blocks.TUncertainty.2273.description.4: 5=Age of data unknown or more than 15 years of difference to the time period of the dataset (fields 600-610)
blocks.TUncertainty.2274.description.1: 2=Average data from larger area in which the area under study is included
blocks.TUncertainty.2274.description.2: 3=Data from area with similar production conditions
blocks.TUncertainty.2274.description.3: 4=Data from are with slightly similar production conditions
blocks.TUncertainty.2274.description.4: 5=Data from unknown OR distinctly different area (north america instead of middle east, OECD-Europe instead of Russia)
blocks.TUncertainty.2275.description.0: 1=Data from enterprises, processes and materials under study
blocks.TUncertainty.2275.description.1: 2=Data from processes and materials under study  (i.e. identical technology) but from different enterprises
blocks.TUncertainty.2275.description.2: 3=Data from processes and materials under study but from different technology
blocks.TUncertainty.2275.description.4: 5=Data on related processes on laboratory scale or from different technology
blocks.TRepresentativeness.intro.0: Contains information about the representativeness of the information in the dataset and about how data have been sampled and/or calculated.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3000.description.0: The system model describes how activity datasets are linked to form product systems. Some options in the ecoinvent network are 'undefined', 'attributional, average current suppliers, revenue allocation', 'consequential, small-scale, long-term decisions'.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3001.description.0: Reference to the context of the system model.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3001.description.1: If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3005.description.0: This is the plaintext value of the referenced system model (field 3000).
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3010.description.0: Percent of data sampled out of the total that the activity is intended to represent (as given by the fields under Geography, Technology and Time Period).
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3030.description.0: Text describing the sampling and calculation procedures applied for quantifying the exchanges. Reports whether the sampling procedure for particular elementary and intermediate exchanges differ from the general procedure. Mentions possible problems in combining different sampling procedures.Text and image fields are list of text, imageUri and variable elements. The text and imageUri elements can used to describe the current section and they can be combined in any order given by their index attribute. Text variables are defined by the variable elements, which may be used in the text as {{variablename}}. If a parent text field includes a variable, this variable may be redefined by the child activity dataset while keeping the rest of the parent text intact. This allows easy changes of text parts in child processes.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3040.description.0: Describes extrapolations of data from another time period, another geographical area or another technology and the way these extrapolations have been carried out.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3040.description.1: It should be reported whether different extrapolations have been done on the level of individual exchanges.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3040.description.2: If data representative for a activity operated in one country is used for another country's activity, its original representativity can be indicated here.
blocks.TRepresentativeness.3040.description.3: Changes in mean values due to extrapolations may also be reported here.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.intro.0: Contains information about who collected, compiled or published the orginal data. This may or may not be the same person as under 'DataEntryBy'. Furthermore contains information about kind of publication underlying the dataset and the accessibility of the dataset.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3500.option: ID number for the data generator, i.e. the person or organisation that collected, compiled or published the original data. This may or may not be the same person as the author (see 'DataEntryBy'). The purpose of this field is to acknowledge and reference the origin of the data and the person or organisation that performed the majority of the work in data collection.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3500.descri: ID number for the person that generated the dataset. It must correspond to an ID number of a person listed in the respective dataset.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3501.descri: Reference to the context of the person.
If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3505.descri: Name and surname of the person.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3506.descri: Complete email address of the person.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3510.option: 0 = Data as such not published elsewhere (default), 1 = The data of some unit processes or subsystems are published, 2 = Data has been published entirely in (refers to field 757)
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3510.descri: Indicates whether the dataset has been published (not, partly, entirely).
The codes are: 0=Data as such not published (default). 1=The data of some unit processes or subsystems are published. 2=Data has been published entirely in 'referenceToPublishedSource'.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3520.descri: ID number for the report in which the dataset is documented.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3521.descri: Reference to the context of the published source.
If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3522.descri: If a reference to a master data entity must be removed in a child dataset it is required to set the corresponding xxxOverwrittenByChild attribute to true. Otherwise the removed referenced will be interpreted as "Keep the Parent Value".
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3525.descri: Indicates the year of publication and communication, respectively. For web-sites: last visited.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3526.descri: Indicates the first author by surname and abbreviated name (e.g., Einstein A.). In case of measurement on site, oral communication, personal written communication and questionnaries ('sourceType'=4, 5, 6, 7) the name of the communicating person is mentioned here.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3530.descri: The relevant page numbers if the data are sourced on specific pages in an article or larger publication.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3540.descri: Indicates whether or not a copyright exists. '1' (Yes) or '0' (No) should be entered correspondingly.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3550.descri: Indicates possible access restrictions for the dataset.
accessRestrictedTo=1: only license holders (as defined by context) have access.
accessRestrictedTo=2: license holders (as defined by context) have access to LCI results but not to unit process raw data. Database administrator have full access.
accessRestrictedTo=3: only the organisation specified by 'companyCode' and the database administrator have access.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3560.descri: Reference to an organisation/institute that the use of this dataset is restricted to.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3561.descri: Reference to the context of the company.
If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself will be used instead.
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3562.descri: Optional 7 letter code plaintext of the referenced company (field 3560)
blocks.TDataGeneratorAndPublication.3563.descri: If a reference to a master data entity must be removed in a child dataset it is required to set the corresponding xxxOverwrittenByChild attribute to true. Otherwise the removed referenced will be interpreted as "Keep the Parent Value".
blocks.TFileAttributes.intro.0: Contains metainformation regarding the file as a whole.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3800.description.0: The major release number is increased by one with each major update (e.g. every second year).
blocks.TFileAttributes.3805.description.0: The minor release number is increased by one for each release within the period of two major updates.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3810.description.0: The revision number is specific to each dataset and is independent of the overall database release version and is used to discern different versions of the dataset within the database major/minor release versions. The major revision number reflects the amount of accepted changes to the dataset. It will only increase over time and must not be changed manually. In the ecoinvent context the major revision is increased each time changes to an activity are added to the database (i.e. after they passed the review process). This also resets the minor revision to 1.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3815.description.0: The minor revision number describes versions of the dataset during the editing process before it is submitted for review. In th eecoinvent context it is increased automatically every time the data provider saves changes made to the dataset either locally or as a draft on the ecoinvent server. The minor revision number is reset to “1” each time the major revision number is increased (when changes to a dataset are accepted by a reviewer).
blocks.TFileAttributes.3820.description.0: Default language for all multi language fields of this dataset. Any multi language field should contain a value at least for the default language. If no defaultLanguage is given, the default value ("en") will be used.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3830.description.0: Automatically generated date when dataset is created.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3840.options: Time of last editing of dataset
blocks.TFileAttributes.3840.description.0: Automatically generated date when dataset is saved.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3850.description.0: Dataset is generated based on this internal schema version.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3860.description.0: Description of the program which created this file. Preferably including version.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3870.description.0: Time and date this file was created.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3880.description.0: Indicates the context for which this dataset is designed. The information is used, e.g. for restricting the accessibility of dataset information to one particular context and to determine which master data files are needed to access it. If this attribute is omitted the dataset is assumed to be a standalone dataset and masterdata references can not be dereferenced.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3880.description.1: The context replaces the ecoSpold01 quality network (field id 304). The context id for the ecoinvent quality network can be found in the Context.xml master data file.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3885.description.0: The name of the context referenced by field 3880.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3885.description.1: The context replaces the ecoSpold01 quality network (field id 304). The context id for the ecoinvent quality network can be found in the Context.xml master data file.
blocks.TFileAttributes.3890.description.0: Reference to a context required to load this document with all its master data references intact.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.intro.0: This type allows to specify which context(s) must be known if a dataset is to be read using the master data referenced by it.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.intro.1: It can be used signal that master data entries from different contexts are needed to read this dataset. The software reading the dataset must be aware of those contexts and must know where to find the actual master data files of each context.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7810.descripti: This version number can be used to make sure that the necessary master data entries are present for an activity.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7820.descripti: This version number can be used to make sure that the necessary master data entries are present for an activity.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7830.descripti: This version number can be used to make sure that the necessary master data entries are present for an activity.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7840.descripti: This version number can be used to make sure that the necessary master data entries are present for an activity.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7850.descripti: Reference to the context of the master data file.
If this attribute is omitted the context of the dataset itself should be used instead.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7855.descripti: The name of the context referenced by field 7850.
blocks.TRequiredContextReference.7860.descripti: Optional URI reference to the directory containing the master data files of this context.
